direct_answer:
BASF integrates sustainability-related performance into remuneration mainly through variable pay for the Board of Executive Directors and senior executives, while Supervisory Board remuneration has no variable component and is therefore not linked to sustainability targets [Source 1].

- Long-term incentive (LTI): BASF anchored the reduction of Group-wide CO2 emissions (Scope 1 and Scope 2) as a key nonfinancial KPI in its steering and compensation systems in 2020 [Source 1]. Reducing Group-wide Scope 1 and 2 CO2 emissions is one of three equally weighted strategic targets (33.3%) for the LTI of the Board of Executive Directors and senior executives [Source 1].

- Short-term incentive (STI) for senior executives in operating business units: In the reporting year, BASF introduced an STI program with targets intended to drive the market-driven transformation [Source 1]. Besides financial targets, the STI includes three additional targets: (i) occupational and process safety, (ii) sustainability, and (iii) development of the operating divisions; the first two are sustainability-related [Source 1]. These three objectives are equally weighted in the STI calculation and together account for 25% of the total STI formula; therefore, 16.7% of the entire STI formula is sustainability-related [Source 1]. The sustainability target includes elements such as sales of Sustainable-Future Solutions and increasing the share of purchased raw materials with supplier-specific Product Carbon Footprints [Source 1].
compliance_rationale: The passages provide key characteristics of the incentive schemes (LTI and STI), identify specific sustainability metrics/targets used (Scope 1&2 CO2 reduction; occupational/process safety; sustainability elements such as Sustainable-Future Solutions sales and supplier-specific PCF share), and quantify the proportion of variable remuneration linked to sustainability for LTI (33.3% weight) and STI (16.7% of formula) [Source 1]. However, the evidence does not specify the governance level at which the terms of these incentive schemes are approved and updated, as required by ESRS 2 GOV-3(e), nor does it fully describe assessment against “impacts” beyond targets/metrics [Source 1].
disclosure_gaps: Level in the undertaking at which the terms of the incentive schemes are approved and updated (ESRS 2 GOV-3(e)) is not stated in the provided passages.
Further detail on how performance is assessed against specific sustainability-related impacts (not only targets/metrics) is not evidenced in the provided passages.

Whether sustainability-related metrics apply to all members of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies beyond the Board of Executive Directors and specified senior executives (scope/coverage details) is not fully evidenced in the provided passages.
key_findings: Reduction of Group-wide Scope 1 and 2 CO2 emissions is a key nonfinancial KPI embedded in BASF’s steering and compensation systems since 2020 [Source 1].
For the Board of Executive Directors and senior executives, Scope 1 and 2 CO2 reduction is one of three equally weighted (33.3%) strategic targets in the long-term incentive (LTI) [Source 1].
Supervisory Board remuneration has no variable components and is not linked to target achievement (including sustainability targets) [Source 1].

In the reporting year, BASF introduced an STI program for senior executives in operating business units with sustainability-related targets; 16.7% of the STI formula is sustainability-related [Source 1].

The STI sustainability target includes elements such as sales of Sustainable-Future Solutions and increasing the share of purchased raw materials with supplier-specific Product Carbon Footprints [Source 1].
